  "id": "SPEC-002",
  "purpose": "Give callisto consumers a working, documented mechanism that places CI-built native binary artifacts (napi-rs .node files, maturin wheels) into their platform-stub package directories before `callisto publish` runs, closing the gap between `callisto matrix`'s output and a working end-to-end release.",
  "scope": "Extends `.github/actions/callisto-action/action.yml`'s existing `callisto-orchestrate` composite-action step: after it computes `nativeMatrix` and before it invokes `callisto plan-publish`/publish (in the branch already gated by `INPUT_PUBLISH`), the step downloads each `nativeMatrix` entry's artifact by `artifactName`, pinned to the current workflow run via `$GITHUB_RUN_ID`, and places its contents into `packageDir`, formalizing `.claude/specs/callisto-matrix.md` §6.2's design.   "non_goals": [
    "Extending PlatformTargetKind to Java/JNI or .NET native-AOT targets — a separate, later concern; this spec only routes the two kinds PlatformTargetKind already supports (Napi, Maturin).",
    "Prebuilt Rust CLI binaries distributed as GitHub Release assets (\"Tier 2\") — a separate, related, deferred future spec.",
    "Homebrew tap formula generation/distribution — deferred by the maintainer as a possible separate future tool.",
    "Go binary distribution — already an existing non-goal per .claude/specs/callisto-matrix.md §8, not being revisited here.",
    "A generic callisto-build-action that dispatches the actual per-platform build (napi build --platform --release, etc.) — callisto-matrix.md §7's secondary/optional proposal. This spec covers only placement of an already-built, correctly-named artifact; the build step itself is the consumer's own responsibility.",
    "Validating the content of a downloaded artifact (e.g. confirming a .node file is well-formed, or that it is actually a valid binary for its target triple). The placement step moves whatever files gh run download retrieves into packageDir; content correctness is the build job's responsibility and surfaces later, at publish or install time, not at placement.",
    "Adding a new required input to callisto-action to opt into placement. Placement is driven entirely by whether nativeMatrix is a non-empty array — consumers with no native platform targets see zero behavior change.",
    "Implementing the nonexistent callisto publish-target Rust CLI subcommand referenced by the current ARCHITECTURE.md §12. That subcommand is not needed for this requirement; publish already works via the existing callisto publish command operating on on-disk state once artifacts are placed.",
    "Guaranteeing that a binary placed at packageDir by this step is picked up and included in callisto publish's registry upload output (npm tarball, PyPI wheel, etc.). That round-trip guarantee is owned by whatever spec governs callisto publish's own native-binary packaging logic (crates/callisto-graph/src/commands/publish.rs) — this spec's guarantee ends at the file being present on disk at packageDir before publish begins. If no spec currently covers that round-trip, closing it is a follow-up dependency of this spec, not an implicit assumption made here."
  ],
  "api_surface": [
    {
      "name": "callisto-action native artifact placement step",
      "signature": "New step inside `.github/actions/callisto-action/action.yml`'s existing `callisto-orchestrate` composite step, sequenced after `NATIVE_MATRIX=$(callisto matrix --format json | jq ...)` is computed and before `callisto plan-publish`/publish executes, inside the branch guarded by `else` (no pending changesets) and further guarded by `[[ -n \"$INPUT_PUBLISH\" ... ]]`",

Runs once per array element, in array order. `gh run download` creates `packageDir` (including any missing parent directories) automatically if it does not already exist on disk, so a not-yet-existing packageDir is not itself an error condition — the step only fails if the named artifact cannot be found within the current run. Skipped entirely (zero `gh run download` invocations) when `nativeMatrix` is `[]`."
    }
  ],
  "acceptance_criteria": [
    {"id": "AC-001", "criterion": "Given a workflow run where N per-platform build jobs each upload an artifact via actions/upload-artifact using the exact artifactName string from that platform's callisto matrix --format json entry, and the callisto-orchestrate step subsequently runs with INPUT_PUBLISH set to a truthy value: after the step completes, each of the N artifacts' downloaded file contents are present under the corresponding packageDir path relative to the working directory (with packageDir having been created automatically by gh run download if it did not already exist), and this placement completes before the step's callisto plan-publish/publish invocation begins.", "is_error_case": false},
    {"id": "AC-002", "criterion": "Given nativeMatrix is [] (no native platform-target packages in the workspace) and INPUT_PUBLISH is set to a truthy value, the callisto-orchestrate step invokes gh run download zero times and proceeds directly to callisto plan-publish/publish exactly as it did before this change.", "is_error_case": false},
    {"id": "AC-003", "criterion": "Given a nativeMatrix entry whose artifactName was never uploaded within the current workflow run ($GITHUB_RUN_ID) -- including the case where an artifact with that exact name exists in a different, older, or unrelated workflow run in the same repository -- the placement loop's `gh run download \"$GITHUB_RUN_ID\" --name \"$ARTIFACT\" --dir \"$DIR\"` invocation exits non-zero because the run-id pins the lookup to the current run only, no same-named artifact from a different run can satisfy it, the step fails (non-zero exit, workflow run marked failed) before reaching callisto plan-publish/publish, and the step's log output names the specific missing artifactName.", "is_error_case": true},
    {"id": "AC-004", "criterion": "Given the nativeMatrix GitHub Actions output value is not valid JSON (e.g. truncated or hand-edited by a caller), the placement loop's jq -c '.[]' parse fails, the step exits non-zero before any gh run download call, and callisto plan-publish/publish is not invoked.", "is_error_case": true},
    {"id": "AC-005", "criterion": "Given a nativeMatrix entry that is syntactically valid JSON but has a missing, null, or empty-string artifactName or packageDir field, the placement loop detects this before invoking gh run download for that entry, the step fails (non-zero exit) with log output identifying which field was missing/null/empty and the zero-based index of the offending entry in the nativeMatrix array, and callisto plan-publish/publish is not invoked.", "is_error_case": true},
    {"id": "AC-006", "criterion": "Two nativeMatrix entries that both name the same artifactName (already deduplicated upstream by unique_by(.artifactName) in the existing NATIVE_MATRIX computation) never both trigger a gh run download call for that name within a single step invocation -- the existing dedup guarantees at most one download attempt per distinct artifactName.", "is_error_case": false},
    {"id": "AC-007", "criterion": "ARCHITECTURE.md §12, read in full, contains no occurrence of the string callisto publish-target anywhere in its text or code blocks.", "is_error_case": false},
    {"id": "AC-008", "criterion": "ARCHITECTURE.md §12's example workflow, read end to end, shows all of: a build job producing and uploading a per-platform artifact, a placement step downloading that artifact into its package directory, and a callisto publish (or callisto-action with publish enabled) step running afterward against the populated package directories -- not just the build step.", "is_error_case": false},
    {"id": "AC-009", "criterion": "A consumer workflow that already uses callisto-action for publishing and adds only a matrix-driven build job (per .claude/specs/callisto-matrix.md §6.1's nativeMatrix consumption pattern) uploading artifacts named per artifactName, with no additional bash, composite action, or script written by the consumer to perform placement, ends with artifacts correctly placed and callisto publish succeeding.", "is_error_case": false}
  ],
  "linked_requirement": "REQ-001"
}
